summary: Configured 512MB compressed (lzo) zram swap on node1 via a custom systemd oneshot unit (zram-swap.service), enabled at boot, with priority 100 so it is preferred over the existing disk-backed swap (/dev/vda2, priority -2). Verified persistence by restarting node1 and confirming boot identity changed and zram swap auto-activated post-restart. RHEL 7.9 has no zram-generator package (that's a RHEL8+/9 tool), so swap was built manually from the in-tree zram kernel module.
actions_performed: Inspected node1: RHEL 7.9, kernel 3.10.0-1160.el7, existing 2G disk swap on /dev/vda2 at priority -2, zram kernel module present (lzo compression only)
Cleaned up a stuck background yum process left over from an earlier timed-out repolist command (killed pids, removed stale /var/run/yum.pid)
Created /etc/modules-load.d/zram.conf to load zram module at boot
Created /etc/systemd/system/zram-swap.service (oneshot, RemainAfterExit) that modprobes zram, sets /sys/block/zram0/disksize=512M, runs mkswap, and swapon -p 100 /dev/zram0; ExecStop does swapoff
Ran systemctl daemon-reload, enabled and started zram-swap.service; verified swapon --show and /proc/swaps show zram0 (512M, lzo, priority 100) ranked above vda2 (priority -2)
Captured pre-restart boot_id and swap state baseline, restarted node1 via sudo shutdown -r now, polled until exec access returned
Confirmed post-restart boot_id differs from baseline (proving an actual reboot occurred) and re-verified zram swap auto-recovered with identical size/algorithm/priority and service enabled+active

evidence.requirement: zram swap >=512MB, compressed, configured and active
evidence.summary: zram-swap.service created and started; swapon --show and /proc/swaps show /dev/zram0 at 512M (524284 KiB) with lzo compression algorithm, mkswap/swapon succeeded

evidence.requirement: zram swap preferred over disk-backed swap
evidence.summary: swapon --show output: /dev/vda2 priority -2 (disk), /dev/zram0 priority 100 (zram) — higher priority means kernel uses zram first

Baseline boot_id 33b0e84c captured before reboot; shutdown -r now issued; post-reboot exec succeeded with uptime '0 min'; post-restart boot_id a6d0ff12 differs from baseline, proving the node actually rebooted; zram-swap.service shown enabled+active and /dev/zram0 present at 512M/lzo/priority 100 identical to pre-restart configuration
